design: Three tasks, two conditions, two fresh independent agents per task and condition. The first retrieval pair preceded the remaining runs. Task, code, engineering documentation, approval history and handoff were matched; workflow integration differed. Same inherited host model and effort; no per-worker override. A coordinator explicitly launched each worker; no autonomous model runner.
interpretation: This is a small descriptive fixture comparison, not evidence of a universal quality gain.
The unavailable plain retrieval attempt changed a protected plan contract by adding verification prose. That format-sensitive rejection does not establish incorrect application behavior.

The failed plain retrieval attempt passed working-tree behavior but claimed commit readiness with failing staged behavior. It is a delivery discrepancy, not a failure to retrieve the application contract.
All scored attempts had zero counted unnecessary approval stops. A passing score does not establish smooth workflow execution or independent review.
Integrated attempts reported finalization friction around protected approval history or staging. The fixture protocol takes precedence over normal workflow instructions.
These runs used the frozen Step 12 executable. Subsequent final-delivery reconciliation changes are covered by separate regression tests, not by these attempts.
limitations: Only two attempts per task and condition; no significance or causal performance claim.

Conditions were not randomized. Some runs overlapped other host work or crossed multi-day session interruptions. Elapsed intervals include observer collection delay and must not be compared as task execution speed.
Per-attempt token counts are unavailable; no token or cost savings were inferred.
Worker review actions are self-reported; the deterministic grader observes files, bindings and stated dispositions.
The harness and some normal workflow instructions disagree over allowed finalization changes; these attempts measure that combined protocol.

Published rows retain sanitized outcomes and integrity digests, not private fixture directories or raw agent transcripts. Repeating the fixture creates a new attempt; reproducing an original score also requires its private initial/final snapshots.
